week-1-day-2.text: I selected a clear channel category or niche.
I researched viral channels in the category.
I checked proof-of-concept signals such as recently sold channels where relevant.
I copied the God prompt into Google Docs and edited its variables.
I ran the research in Kimi.
I reviewed Section A of the research report.
I captured the unique value proposition, tagline and mission statement.
I created a channel profile picture using the Section B inputs.
I created a YouTube channel banner in Canva.
I am ready to move toward launching the channel.

week-2-day-1.text: I completed the Day 1 Shot / Frame Breakdown.
I recorded my Generation Tool(s) and Character / Visual Consistency Notes.
I tracked the clips or frames I generated and updated the Combined Video Status.
I generated at least one usable shot from a frame and prompt.
I know how to use the frame workflow in Flow.
I created or prepared a voiceover for my shot.
I created a first draft of my timeline.
I published my shot for today.
I have a plan to publish one shot every day for the next seven days.
I will observe the winners and use them to guide my next shots.

week-2-day-2.text: I completed the remaining image practice from Day 2.
I generated the aerial coconut-farm shot.
I generated the close-up coconut bunch shot.
I generated the coconut falling shot.
I completed the other required frames and posted them in the group.
I created at least one image-to-video shot from a strong frame.
I used Start and End Frame Animation only when the frames had a meaningful visual relationship.
I used start-frame-only when an end frame would create an unrelated transition.
I checked continuity, movement and product consistency in my generated clips.
I selected keepers before spending credits on higher-quality output.

week-3-day-1.text: I selected and prepared useful character references.
I created a character sheet in Flow.
I fixed or documented any face-consistency issue.
I generated and selected a brand colour palette in Gemini.
I created a mood board in Flow.
I attached the character sheet and mood board to the screenplay workflow.
I generated and reviewed the screenplay.
I converted the screenplay into a structured shot shortlist.
I organized the assets and project documents for continued production.
I understand the three-failure rule and when to change the generation approach.

week-3-day-2.text: Hero face and costume remain recognizable across the character sheet and chosen shots.
Raw personal reference photos are kept out of cohort-group submissions.
The hero base reads as one coherent, recognizable location.
Title artwork is legible and has a clean transparent background.
The edit includes a purposeful establishing moment, reveal, and action beat where available.
Chosen supporting shots fit the hero and location continuity.
The project is saved and the exported teaser plays with intentional title and audio choices.
Only the finished teaser is submitted, and public audio is owned or licensed for use.

week-4-day-1.text: Character face, costume and anatomy remain consistent across the approved reference sheet.
Architecture references describe one recognizable location from useful angles.
Title asset is readable and exported as a clean transparent PNG.
A-roll keeps the intended hero and location across the selected moments.
Every B-roll shot supports a specific editing need.
The saved 16:9 timeline has a clear reveal, clean cuts and intentional sound.
The exported teaser plays from beginning to end and only finished media is submitted.

week-4-day-2.text: The approved phone references show the correct model, camera geometry, ports and proportions.
The selected still frames preserve the same phone and camera layout across the shot list.
Motion clips use the demonstrated start-frame, end-frame or start-only method for each shot.
The cut uses no more than five core shots and remains ten seconds before any optional outro.
The edit uses clean cuts and only purposeful speed changes, music and sound effects.
The exported file plays from beginning to end with consistent colour, geometry and synchronized sound.
The saved Homework record contains the final film link and supporting production proof.

week-5-day-1.text: The team selected and can link the property reference images used.
The generated stills and motion clips keep the property recognizable and its architecture stable.
Image-to-video movement is purposeful; the team fixed or removed shots with visible warping or unusable transitions.
The Filmora edit forms one clear walkthrough with music and avoids unnecessary beauty-shot filler.
The team produced one final video that is about one minute or less.

week-5-day-2.text: The screenplay follows the assigned story and is approved before shot listing.
Every shot has a clear visual action and camera choice.
Lighting and color stay consistent across the production sheet.
Main characters and important props have references where needed.
Image-generation and video-generation leads reviewed the plan together.
Dialogue and voiceover are planned without relying on long monologues.

week-6-day-1.text: I confirmed my team and the film/topic assigned to us.
I listed only the characters that appear in our assigned film.
I used the supplied face and costume references when revising character sheets.
The character sheets include consistent views and useful expressions.
I checked the Mahabharatha Project (BMAM) sheet and shot list for story-critical props.
Each prop reference is tied to a character or scene, and unknown details are marked for review.
I recorded a visible mismatch before revising an image or clip.
I compared the selected generation with the supplied references.
I checked scale, anatomy, movement, and continuity before approving motion.
I shared the approved sheets, versions, open issues, and next owner with the team.
I kept the Mahabharata treatment respectful and avoided spoof framing.

week-6-day-2.text: One named character is saved and selected for reuse.
The 9:16 product-in-hand frame keeps character, packaging, and label details consistent.
The A-roll uses the approved dialogue, audio, and product image as its start frame only.
The spoken claims are verified and authorized; face, teeth, hands, and product contact look stable.
B-roll adds useful product detail and keeps the product and lighting consistent.
The 9:16 edit has clear dialogue, restrained transitions, useful audio, and a reviewed export.

week-7-day-1.text: I prepared a clean portrait from my previous multi-angle photos and checked the likeness.
I used a new Flow project and selected Nano Banana Pro for the uploaded character image.
I added a template voice to the Flow character and previewed its sample dialogue.
I tagged the saved character and checked the Agent scene breakdown before generation.
I reviewed the Agent model, aspect ratio, variation count, approval setting, and credit request.
I completed the video avatar consent and identity verification steps for my own likeness.
I reviewed identity, voice, dialogue, lip movement, framing, and generated text in both tests.
I recorded the result links, comparison, first fix, and portfolio next step in the Homework Doc.

week-7-day-2.text: I chose a builder and tailored the master prompt to my actual portfolio.
I reviewed the proposed pages and interactions before generating the site.
I replaced the available project, profile, video, and service placeholders with accurate material.
I checked navigation, project filtering, video playback, and the requested interactions.
I reviewed the desktop and mobile layouts and recorded anything unavailable or broken.
I saved the preview or published link and my first grouped revision priorities in the Homework Doc.

week-8-day-1.text: I chose a four-wheel vehicle and gathered same-colour references from useful angles.
I checked that the vehicle's distinguishing body details remain consistent in my generated images.
I planned an ordered set of advertisement shots with a clear camera move for each.
I used start and end frames only when they show a coherent continuation of the same vehicle and scene.
I reviewed vehicle identity, camera path, wheel rotation, background motion, and road or water behavior in each clip.
I assembled a linked advertisement draft and recorded one issue and the first next fix in the Homework Doc.

week-8-day-2.text: I chose one transformation and identified the base clip or frame.
I wrote what must change and what should remain stable in the shot.
I prepared and labelled the reference assets required by the selected workflow.
I selected a source-backed method and attached the intended video, image, prop, character or background references.
I reviewed the generated clip for subject identity, scene continuity, camera, timing, lighting and motion drift.
I saved the selected output and its source/reference links in the official Homework Doc.
I recorded one observed problem and a first correction that addresses it.

week-7-day-3.text: I preserved the rough cut and saved a separate working project with linked source media.
I checked the project frame shape and retained only usable footage ranges.
I reviewed shot order, motion continuity and every repaired join.
I made a deliberate rhythm decision; ramps or natural speed support the scene.
I checked keyframed graphics or the chosen static treatment for clarity and safe placement.
I balanced the required audio layers and verified speech or ambience transitions.
I checked colour consistency and all retained titles or captions.
I watched the actual exported file from beginning to end with sound.
I saved the final film, editable project and before/after evidence in the Homework Doc.
I recorded any remaining issue and followed the current cohort submission instructions.
